speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have a longstanding pruritic rash with numbness and tingling on your palms. To narrow down the cause, how long have these symptoms been present, and has the rash appeared on any other parts of your body?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of an itchy rash on his upper body and face. Additionally, he has been experiencing a numbness and tingling sensation on both palms. He has been working on his family's rice farm, also caring for livestock.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Dirofilaria immitis (Heartworm) or similar filarial infection; however, the clinical picture of pruritic rash, acral neuropathy, and history of livestock/rice farm exposure is most consistent with chronic arsenic poisoning (arsenical keratosis/neuropathy) or potentially a specific tropical infection like Onchocerciasis or Chagas disease. Given the specific combination of palm paresthesia and widespread pruritic rash with agricultural exposure, I will proceed with the following plan:
